records.title: Finish Him — How Commander Combos Actually End
records.description: Across 15,107 documented lethal Commander combo variants, most don't end with one dramatic final move — they end with the game handing you a loop and saying: do it again. A Magic Math data story.

records.title: The Mana Base Codex · All 37 Commander Identities
records.description: An illuminated reference to every Commander mana-fixing land and rock, mapped across all 37 color identities — with a hypergeometric consistency lab, a chronological timeline of fixing, and an authored lore layer.

records.title: GQM Goal-Question-Metric Mapping Worksheet
records.description: A one-pager: map each dashboard goal through a diagnostic question to the one or two metrics that actually answer it, then audit anything already on the dashboard against the chain.

records.title: Quality, Translated
records.description: A one-page reference: the same release risk shown three ways — what an executive, a product owner, and an engineer each need to see.

records.title: Risk-Based Regression Triage Sheet
records.description: A one-pager: the five inputs that build a risk-based regression model, plus the two safety nets that keep it honest.

records.title: Static Site Launch-Readiness Check
records.description: A one-page checklist for static sites: make each invisible seam — third-party calls, metadata, data drift, forms, client JS — visible on the deployed URL before you point a domain at it.

records.title: Test Pyramid Assessment Generator
records.description: An offline browser tool for assessing automated test portfolio shape, surfacing likely risks, and exporting a Markdown or text report for a test-strategy review.

records.title: It's Not Your Automation Tool That's Broken — It's Your Process
records.description: Teams blame the framework when nightly runs go red and tests get flaky. Most of the time the framework isn't the problem — nobody owns the suite. Here's what changes when you fix that instead of rewriting it.

records.title: How I Cut a Regression Cycle in Half
records.description: Our platform upgraded twice a year, and testing one upgrade in full took three months. Here's the method that cut it to six weeks: an honest audit, a coverage map, a business-built rubric, vendor guidance, and ISTQB-style risk scoring.

records.title: How I Run AI Like a QA System
records.description: AI is non-deterministic by design. I run my AI work the way I run quality engineering: operating prompts, grounding, examples, gates, and feedback loops.

records.title: Izzet and Prismari Are Both Blue-Red. They're Not the Same Deck.
records.description: Same two colors, same color pie, completely different game. Izzet and Prismari prove that a color identity tells you the toolbox, not which tool gets picked up twice a turn.

records.title: A Quiz Can Be Evidence, Not Vibes
records.description: Most fandom quizzes hand you a confident label and no receipts. Building voxmana.io's placement quiz, I built the other kind — one that tracks its evidence, resolves the near-miss, and refuses to call a vibe a fact.

records.title: Your QA Dashboard Doesn't Need More Charts, It Needs Fewer Questions
records.description: Most QA dashboards get built bottom-up from whatever the tools export, which is how they end up full of vanity metrics nobody acts on. The Goal-Question-Metric framework flips the build order.

records.title: Static Doesn’t Mean Safe — What Building voxmana.io Taught Me
records.description: Building voxmana.io as a static site didn't remove release risk — it hid it in the seams. Here's where a 'static' side project can still bite, and how I made those risks visible before launch.

records.title: Traceable Isn't the Same as True
records.description: A v1 launch scan on Vox Mana came back green — records existed, citations resolved, generated pages matched their source, regression passed. Exploratory testing found the checks were proving the wrong thing anyway. Here's the gap, and the rule I use to close it.

records.title: What Good QA Actually Owns
records.description: QA owns quality — and you own it by making it visible to the right people, in the language they can act on, before it ships.

records.title: The Ages of Fixing: What Every Magic Land Is Charging You
records.description: Thirty years of Magic land design is one long argument about a single question: how easy should it be to cast your spells on time? Read the lands as answers and it starts to make sense.

records.title: Your Precon Is a Passport
records.description: A precon isn't a lesser deck you apologize for — it's the fastest legal way into a Commander game. The nerves aren't the problem. Not having four sentences ready is.

records.title: Your Test Pyramid Is an Umbrella — and It Is Costing You
records.description: An 87% UI automation portfolio does not prove strong coverage. It proves the slowest, most expensive layer is carrying work that should be split across API, contract, component, and unit checks.

records.title: MTG Store Inventory App Concept
records.description: Inventory ingestion, pricing, condition tracking, and local game store support.

records.title: Recipe Flexibility App Concept
records.description: Recipe adaptation for cookware, substitutions, time, and family constraints.

records.title: Vox Mana
records.description: A live, source-governed Commander discovery tool — enterprise QA habits at hobby scale.
